nodes.description: Brain RNA-seq of homozygous Dip2c knockout mice found 838 differentially expressed genes, enriched for memory and neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction and including several glutamate and GABA receptor subunit genes. How DIP2C regulates these genes, and whether the same changes occur in heterozygous human brain, is unknown.

meta.association: Heterozygous DIP2C variants are the defining cause. In the 23-patient cohort the variants were nonsense, frameshift and canonical splice-site alleles predicted to cause loss of function, plus two de novo missense variants; ten patients had de novo variants and nine had inherited ones. Earlier reports include a de novo canonical splice-acceptor variant in a child ascertained for childhood apraxia of speech (later included as patient 14 of the 23-patient cohort), and a de novo splice-site variant in an infant with focal epilepsy. A high-impact DIP2C frameshift was also prioritized in a Swedish cohort with severe developmental language disorder. A 67.6 kb mosaic deletion removing at least two DIP2C exons, classed as a variant of uncertain significance, was found in two children with hemiplegic cerebral palsy, one of whom also had a middle cerebral artery infarction. No ClinGen gene-disease validity record exists for DIP2C.

nodes.description: Most disease alleles are nonsense, frameshift or canonical splice-site variants predicted to undergo nonsense-mediated decay or to disrupt splicing, so the proposed lesion is loss of one functional DIP2C copy. Two de novo missense variants were also reported and their effect is unknown. DIP2C is expressed most highly in the human neocortex in mid-gestation, which places the dosage loss in the period of cortical development. Across the conserved DIP2 family, the acyl-CoA synthetase (fatty acyl-AMP ligase-like) domains regulate a specific subset of diacylglycerols; whether DIP2C does this in human neurons has not been tested.

nodes.description: CRISPR/Cas9 Dip2c knockout used for brain RNA-seq. The defining human cohort paper reports that the RNA-seq compared homozygous Dip2c delta 2bp male mice at postnatal day 10 with wild-type controls.

Germline Dip2c mutant mice studied at both dosages. Homozygotes show weight loss, hyperlocomotion, cognitive impairment and abnormal lipid metabolism; heterozygotes, the genotype matching the human disease, show only mild cognitive impairment.

The core feature. The defining cohort describes all 23 patients as having developmental delay mainly affecting expressive language and articulation; delayed speech is tabulated in 15 of 16 with data, and first words came after 14 months in 12 of 19.

evidence.snippet: We present 23 individuals with heterozygous DIP2C variants, all manifesting developmental delays that primarily affect expressive language and speech articulation.

nodes.description: Morpholino knockdown of zebrafish dip2ca disrupts cardiac looping, with a linear heart tube, pericardial oedema and arrhythmia, and is partly rescued by wild-type dip2ca mRNA. The study proposed DIP2C as the gene behind congenital heart defects in 10p15.3 microdeletions; structural heart defects also occur in a minority of patients with intragenic DIP2C variants.

evidence.reference_title: The deficiency of DIP2C leads to congenital heart defects in patients with 10p15.3 microdeletion syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Coinjection of wild-type dip2ca mRNA with dip2ca-MO partially rescued these detects.

nodes.description: In Dip2c mutant mouse cortex, expression of a key subunit of serine palmitoyltransferase, the rate-limiting enzyme of sphingolipid synthesis, is raised and sphingolipid metabolism is upregulated. This fits the acyl-CoA synthetase domain of DIP2C but has not been examined in patients.

evidence.reference_title: DIP2C Deficiency Leads to Abnormal Sphingolipid Metabolism in Mice.
evidence.snippet: This effect was likely due to increased expression of a key subunit of serine palmitoyltransferase, the rate-limiting enzyme in sphingolipid biosynthesis.

nodes.description: Dip2c mutant mouse cortex shows increased oligodendrocyte generation and myelination alongside the sphingolipid change. Homozygous mutants were more severely affected than heterozygotes, which showed only mild cognitive impairment. Not yet examined in patients.
